text:
ops-bot: ALERT: SLO breach detected on /v1/streaming (hosted-prod) — p95=420ms (target 200ms), p99=2.8s (target 1s). Increase in streaming stalls and tail latency observed. auto-escalation -> #incidents.

emily: seeing the same from dashboards. streaming stalls spike around 12:10 UTC. p95 jump corresponds to deploy ~11:50 UTC.

raj: quick triage — is this an inference runtime issue or caching? I see error rates are flat (0.01%) so likely latency not errors.

sre_maria: cache metrics: prefix-cache hit rate dropped from ~78% -> 6% for the last hour. KV prefix miss count up x15.

emily: that aligns with prefix cache miss hypothesis. any recent changes to prefix hashing or cache invalidation?

raj: I deployed a prefix-hash change in canary at 11:48 to support new model variants (prefix-hash v3). Canary looked fine but we pushed to prod at 11:52.

product-jane: customers reporting slow responses in streaming sessions (lots of partial-frame stalls). No 5xx yet but UX is bad. One enterprise customer (acme-corp) flagged latency in support.

ops-bot: INCIDENT DETAILS:
- service: streaming-inference
- rooted at: 1887654321
- severity: sev2 (SLO breach, customer impact)
- initial alert: p99 > 2s for 10m

emily: hypothesis: prefix-hash change invalidated existing prefix cache keys. runtime now missing cached prefixes and re-computing leading to cold K/V hits and longer tails on initial tokens.

raj: confirm with logs — fetching recent cache keys and prefix-hash header.

sre_maria: logs snippet:
```
[11:49:02] prefix_hash_version: 2 -> 3
[11:52:08] cache_lookup(prefix=\"the customer said\") -> MISS
[11:52:08] compute_prefix_kv -> 124ms
[11:52:09] stream_push -> stall 540ms
[12:05:12] cache_hit_rate(prefix-cache)=6.3%
```

emily: confirms version bump then widespread misses. Also seeing higher tokenization time on first chunk because KV cache warmed less.

raj: mitigation options: rollback prefix-hash to v2, or add backward-compat fallback to compute with v2 lookup, or bulk warm cache (expensive). Which is fastest?

sre_maria: fastest: toggle runtime feature-flag to enable backward-compat lookup (tries v3 then falls back to v2 keys). Should reduce misses quickly. Rollback is riskier if other services rely on v3 keys.

emily: agreed. do the flag flip first, warm small sample of hot prefixes. If no improvement in 10m, plan rollback.

raj: executing flag flip. command: 
```
# flip prefix hash fallback flag
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/flags/prefix_hash_fallback -d '{"enabled":true}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
```

sre_maria: done. flag set to true at 12:18 UTC.

emily: watching dashboards... p95 down to 210ms, p99 to 1.05s. cache hit rate creeping up to 18%.

product-jane: reporting to support: temporary mitigation in place, monitoring. sending note to acme-corp. :thumbsup:

raj: next step: warm top prefixes to speed recovery. I'll run a warm job for top-1k prefixes.

sre_maria: warming job started (batch fetch + populate). logs: warming 1000 prefixes; estimated 4m to populate hot shards.

ops-bot: SYSTEM: warming-job-1887654321 started by raj.

emily: good sign. p99 now 880ms and trending down. streaming stall traces show fewer stall-sensitive frames.

raj: decision log: (1) enable fallback flag (12:18 UTC) — mitigated immediate SLO breach, (2) run warming job (12:20 UTC) — accelerating hit-rate recovery, (3) no immediate rollback.

sre_maria: additional short-term tweak: increase prefix-cache TTL from 30m -> 120m for hot shards to reduce churn during recovery. applied at 12:26 UTC.

emily: confirm telemetry: prefix-cache hit = 64% after 7m of warming. p95/p99 back within SLOs.

product-jane: advising support to mark incident as mitigated and monitor customer tickets.

raj: root cause (preliminary): unsafe prefix-hash rollout to prod caused cache key mismatch and large-scale cold misses. Change was validated in canary but global key space difference not caught.

sre_maria: impact summary (prelim): ~30-40% of streaming sessions saw tail latency degradation between 11:52-12:18 UTC. No increase in error rate. Estimated ~18k affected requests.

emily: oncall handoff: I'm passing to @luis for next shift to run postmortem and long-term fix (graceful key migration or dual-write during rollout).

luis: taking this. I'll own postmortem, timeline, and action items. Planned follow-ups:
- implement zero-downtime prefix-hash migration strategy (dual-key lookups + background backfill)
- add automated canary test that simulates cache-key space changes
- improve deploy checklist to include cache-migration plan for hash changes

ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated at 12:30 UTC. p99 < 1s for last 5m.

raj: leaving notes for postmortem: commands run, flags toggled, warming job ID, affected shard list.

emily: assigning postmortem owner -> luis. ETA for preliminary postmortem: EOD today.

luis: acknowledged. tagging owners: raj (deploy), sre_maria (cache metrics & warming), emily (runtime tracing), product-jane (customer comms).

ops-bot: Handoff recorded. Next oncall: luis.

sre_maria: saving relevant dashboards and traces: https://grafana.internal/d/streaming/prefix-cache-1887654321

emily: closing on-call work here. leave thread for postmortem comments. good catch everyone. :heart:
